paragraphs: R’ Akiva ben Doma [ben Dosa in the photographed print].

Hyman says the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 1, chapter 2, mentions him as living in the time of R’ Meir and his colleagues. But the version designated כ״ג and Seder HaChachamim read R’ Yaakov ben Dosai, which Hyman considers correct.

notes.text: The source heading has Doma; the metadata has Dosa; the proposed alternative is Yaakov ben Dosai. The edition abbreviated כ״ג remains unidentified.

Both returned evidence records bind the same whole Oxford1888 SederHaChachamim1:12 scalar and raw witness, not independent editions. It lists abbreviated R' Yaakov ben Dosai among Meir’s contemporaries. Hyman’s heading Akiva ben Doma, catalog Dosa, and named Dosai stay distinct. Supplied כ״ג remains unresolved alongside older OCR ב״ג; it is not proved a manuscript siglum. Hyman considers the Yaakov reading correct, at the full force of והוא נכון. No newly inspected full-title witness licenses expanding the exact abbreviated names to Rabbi.

The photographed heading reads ben Dosa, alongside ben Doma in the supplied Hebrew. The Oxford Epistle text on page 6 has Yaakov ben Dosai, and note 12 records Akiva as the reading of the edition designated E., which Neubauer identifies as the Constantinople first edition. Mamo’s text has Yaakov ben Dosa and reports the alternate Akiva ben Dosa. The siglum in Hyman’s scan looks like ב״ג, beside supplied כ״ג. The edition he intended and whether these names refer to the same person remain open.
